rawCommits.subject: fix(terminal): make `clear`/Ctrl+L actually clear the in-app terminal
rawCommits.body:
Windows PowerShell 5.1's `Clear-Host` calls `[Console]::Clear()`, which
routes through Win32 console APIs. Over the portable_pty ConPTY pipe to
xterm.js the translation is imperfect (the visible viewport isn't
always fully wiped) and never emits `ESC[3J`, so the 100k-line xterm.js
scrollback survives — leaving old output sitting one scroll-up away
from a "cleared" screen.

Override `Clear-Host` at PowerShell spawn so it writes the standard VT
reset sequences (`ESC[H ESC[2J ESC[3J`) directly. Compatible with both
PS 5.1 (uses `[char]27` instead of the 6+-only backtick-e) and PS 7.
Since `cls` is just an alias for `Clear-Host`, both commands are fixed.

Also add a Ctrl+L safety net in XTerminal that calls `xterm.clear()`
locally so scrollback is wiped instantly regardless of shell — covers
cmd.exe, broken profiles, and the remote-agent terminal where the
spawn-time override doesn't apply.

rawCommits.subject: fix(terminal): disable PSReadLine prediction to stop history-nav garbling
rawCommits.body:
PSReadLine's inline prediction (greyed-out completion at the end of the
line) emits a mix of cursor-save / selective-erase / cursor-restore VT
sequences on every keystroke. When navigating history with Up/Down those
redraws don't clean up cleanly in xterm.js — fragments of previous
predictions and longer history entries pile up on top of the current
line, especially after the line has wrapped, producing the overlapping
garbled text you see scrolling history.

Extend our PowerShell `-Command` init to:
  - Import-Module PSReadLine (no-op if already loaded).
  - Set-PSReadLineOption -PredictionSource None (kills the overlay).
  - Set-PSReadLineOption -BellStyle None (avoids Tab pings).

Each `Set-PSReadLineOption` call is wrapped in its own try/catch because
PSReadLine 2.0 (the default on Windows PowerShell 5.1) doesn't recognize
`-PredictionSource` and unknown parameters are *terminating* errors that
`-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` cannot suppress. Wrapping individually
lets the BellStyle option still apply on PSReadLine 2.0.

`Nav { loading: true }` and the client cleared `navError` on it, so the
user saw Chromium's native "Hmmm... can't reach this page" / Edge cloud
page instead of our themed overlay.

Stop auto-clearing on background `Nav` events; instead route every
user-driven navigation (URL submit, detected-URL pick, back/forward,
address-bar reload, overlay Reload) through a single `clearNavErrorAnd`
helper that drops the overlay only when the user actually retries.

returned. `about:blank` is special-cased by Chromium and emits no

rawCommits.subject: fix(terminal): defer PTY spawn until first fit and remove PSReadLine
rawCommits.body:
Two compounding fixes for the in-app terminal's cursor-jumping /
overlapping-text bugs on Windows:

1. Defer the PTY spawn until xterm.js has measured its container.
   `useTerminal` no longer auto-spawns on mount; instead it exposes a
   `spawn(cols, rows)` method that XTerminal invokes from its first
   `scheduleFit` callback. Subsequent fits keep going through `resize`
   as before. This guarantees PowerShell + ConPTY start at the real
   buffer width instead of the hard-coded 80x24, so PSReadLine and
   prompt redraws never have to re-anchor against a stale size.

2. Remove PSReadLine on spawn. The PowerShell `-Command` init now runs
   `Remove-Module PSReadLine -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`,
   forcing PowerShell back to its built-in console-host line editor.
   PSReadLine maintains its own model of buffer width / wrap state and
   redraws the current line with cursor-save / selective-erase /
   cursor-restore VT sequences on every keystroke; whenever that model
   disagrees with what xterm.js rendered (multi-line wrapped output,
   long history entries, recently-resized terminal) the redraws stack
   fragments of previous content on top of the current line. Falling
   back to the basic editor trades tab completion / Ctrl+R / syntax
   highlighting for redraws that just work.

Tests:
 - `crates/aura-os-terminal`: replace the PSReadLine-prediction test
   with one asserting `Remove-Module PSReadLine` is in the init and
   that `Set-PSReadLineOption` no longer appears.
 - `interface/src/hooks/use-terminal.test.ts`: every test now calls
   `result.current.spawn(...)` explicitly. New regression test asserts
   the API is not hit until `spawn()` is called, plus an idempotency
   test that a second `spawn()` is a no-op.
 - `interface/src/components/XTerminal/XTerminal.test.tsx`: stub hook
   gains a `spawn` mock; new test asserts spawn fires exactly once
   after the first fit with the proposed dimensions, and the existing
   resize tests assert spawn-then-resize ordering.

rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): probe rustup toolchain dir directly so Homebrew shim stops failing macos-latest
rawCommits.body:
dtolnay/rust-toolchain only adds `${CARGO_HOME}/bin` to `$PATH` when it
has to install rustup itself. On macos-latest (rustup preinstalled by
Homebrew) that branch is skipped, so `~/.cargo/bin/rustc` never exists
and PATH still resolves `rustc` to `/opt/homebrew/bin/rustc`, which is a
chain of symlinks ending at `rustup-init`. Invoked under that name it
just prints `rustup-init 1.29.0` instead of proxying, defeating the
existing CARGO_HOME / `rustup which` / PATH-walk fallbacks.

Add a probe that walks `${RUSTUP_HOME}/toolchains/<toolchain>/bin/rustc`
directly, prefers a directory matching the configured RUST_VERSION, and
reject any candidate whose basename looks like `rustup-init` so we never
re-enter the broken shim. Also update the failure hint to point at
RUSTUP_HOME so future regressions surface the right knob.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): pin rust toolchain bin dir on PATH so Homebrew shim stops swallowing cargo on macos-latest
rawCommits.body:
The previous fix kept the Node parity gate happy by resolving rustc out
of `${RUSTUP_HOME}/toolchains/<toolchain>/bin/`, but the workflow's own
bash steps still ran plain `cargo build ...` and got intercepted by
`/opt/homebrew/bin/cargo` -- another `rustup-init` symlink that fails
with `unexpected argument 'build' found` because it doesn't proxy under
that name. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` only adds `$CARGO_HOME/bin` to
$PATH on its install branch, which is skipped whenever rustup is
preinstalled (i.e. always on macos-latest).

Wrap the dtolnay step in a new composite action,
`./.github/actions/setup-rust-toolchain`, that prepends the resolved
`${RUSTUP_HOME}/toolchains/<toolchain>/bin` directory to `$GITHUB_PATH`
after install. The toolchain version is parsed from
`rust-toolchain.toml` (falling back to `1.94.1`) and matched
case-insensitively against directory names like
`1.94.1-x86_64-apple-darwin`, so every cargo / rustc / rustdoc /
clippy-driver invocation in subsequent steps now resolves to a real
toolchain binary instead of the Homebrew shim. Linux and Windows runners
are unaffected -- the prepended directory just contains the same
binaries those PATHs already pointed at.

Replace all seven `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.94.1` usages across
`desktop-validate.yml`, `release-nightly.yml`, and `release-stable.yml`
with the new composite action.

rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): scrub stale rust-src and disable rustup auto-install to stop CI race
rawCommits.body:
Defends against rust-lang/rustup#988. A prior toolchain dir on the runner
(image, prior job, or older revision of the workflow) leaves a populated
lib/rustlib/src tree, and parallel sccache rustc invocations later race
the rustup proxy into reinstalling rust-src concurrently, surfacing as
"failed to install component: 'rust-src', detected conflict:
'lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/Cargo.lock'" and a downstream "could not
compile quote (build script)". We never need rust-src, so the setup
action now nukes the stale dir before dtolnay runs and exports
RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 so the proxy never tries to mutate toolchain state
during the parallel build.

messaging UX. Phase 1 already landed in the sibling aura-harness repo

agent B via `cross_agent_hook::deliver_message`, the harness now sends

`POST /api/agents/:agent_id/events/stream` and
`POST /api/projects/:project_id/agents/:agent_instance_id/events/stream`.

This change teaches aura-os-server to accept that field and thread it
onto the persistence context so later phases can act on it. Concretely:

- `dto::SendChatRequest` gains an `#[serde(default)] originating_agent_id:
  Option<String>`. `#[serde(default)]` preserves wire compatibility with
  pre-Phase-1 harness builds; the cross-repo contract is documented on
  the field's doc-comment.
- `handlers::agents::chat::persist::ChatPersistCtx` gains a parallel
  `originating_agent_id: Option<String>` field with a doc-comment
  pointing back to the harness `cross_agent_hook::deliver_message`.

  `setup_agent_chat_persistence` wrapper) accept the new

  through. The reset endpoints and the image / 3D generation persist
  paths pass `None` — they are not cross-agent turns.
- `persist_task::run_persist_loop` gains a `tracing::debug!` breadcrumb
  on entry under `target = "aura::cross_agent"`, logging `session_id`,
  `project_agent_id`, and `originating_agent_id`. Phase 6 observability

`ctx.originating_agent_id` and posts agent B's reply back into agent A's

  exercises the integration: when a non-`None` sender flows into

What was added:
- New `cross_agent_reply.rs` module with the constants
  `MAX_CROSS_AGENT_REPLY_DEPTH = 4` and
  `MAX_CROSS_AGENT_REPLY_BYTES = 16 * 1024`, plus the pure helpers
  `truncate_for_cross_agent_reply` and `should_send_cross_agent_reply`
  and the fire-and-forget `spawn_cross_agent_reply_callback`.
- Cycle-depth guard: every server-issued reply POST stamps
  `X-Aura-Cross-Agent-Depth: depth + 1` on the outbound; both chat
  routes (`agent_route::send_agent_event_stream` and
  `instance_route::send_event_stream`) read the header off the
  inbound `HeaderMap` and thread it onto a new
  `ChatPersistCtx.cross_agent_depth: u32` field. Once the chain hits
  `MAX_CROSS_AGENT_REPLY_DEPTH` the callback short-circuits with a
  `tracing::warn!` on the `aura::cross_agent` target.
- Single-hop fall-off: the body's `originating_agent_id` is
  serialized as JSON `null` so the receiver of an auto-reply has no
  upstream to bounce back to. Combined with the depth guard this is
  belt-and-suspenders against ping-pong loops.
- UTF-8-safe truncation: replies above 16 KiB are pruned at the
  largest valid char boundary <= the cap and a visible
  `\n\n[... truncated to 16 KiB by aura-os-server cross-agent reply ...]`
  suffix is appended so the receiving LLM can see the cut.
- Reply text source: the existing `text_delta` accumulator in
  `persist_task_dispatch::handle_text_delta` already populates
  `PersistTaskState.full_text` for the whole turn; `run_persist_loop`
  just clones it into the callback after
  `publish_assistant_message_end_event` succeeds (and skips when
  `saw_error` is true).
- HTTP plumbing: reuses `ChatPersistTaskExtras.http_client`
  (cloned out of `AppState.http_client`) and the inbound `ctx.jwt`
  for bearer auth. Self-base URL is sourced from the existing
  `aura_os_integrations::control_plane_api_base_url()` helper
  (env-driven, no new vars); a `tracing::warn!` notes when the
  loopback fallback was used so a swarm deployment without
  `AURA_SERVER_BASE_URL` / `VITE_API_URL` is grep-able.

What was deliberately NOT done:
- No retry on non-2xx / network error. Cross-agent reply delivery is
  fire-and-forget: the receiving LLM can call `send_to_agent` again
  if it cares, which re-arms the chain with a fresh sender id.
- Single hop only by default. The auto-reply chain dies after one
  POST unless the receiving agent's LLM actively re-arms it; the
  depth header is the safety net for the rare legitimate hand-off
  pattern (A→B→A→B).
- No event_bus.rs WS publisher changes (Phase 4).
- No `interface/` TypeScript changes (Phase 5).
- No end-to-end integration test (Phase 7) — Phase 3 keeps tests at
  the unit level so compile time stays bounded.

rawCommits.subject: refactor(ws): unify chat event payloads and pin WS wire shape
rawCommits.body:
Phase 4 of the send_to_agent cross-agent UX fix locks down the
WebSocket wire shape that the upcoming Phase 5 frontend matcher
keys on, and removes a long-standing drift risk between the two
canonical chat lifecycle publishers.

Motivation
----------
publish_user_message_event and publish_assistant_message_end_event
each owned a separate serde_json::json! builder. The two payloads
had already drifted in subtle ways (extra event_id vs message_id,
divergent comments) and any future change touching one builder but
not the other would silently break cross-agent live-refresh -- the
UI matcher branches on `type` then assumes the rest of the keys
exist, so an elided field looks indistinguishable from an unrelated
event. We need ONE source of truth for the wire shape.

What changed
------------
1. event_bus.rs: introduced a typed `ChatEventPayload<'a>` struct
   and a private `publish_chat_event(bus, event_type, ctx)` helper.
   Both public publishers now delegate to it. The canonical wire
   shape is exactly five keys -- `type`, `session_id`, `project_id`,
   `project_agent_id`, `agent_id` -- with the three id fields as
   `Option<&str>` (no `skip_serializing_if`) so a missing id
   serializes as JSON `null` rather than being elided. Phase 2's
   server-side bookkeeping fields (`originating_agent_id`,
   `cross_agent_depth`) intentionally do NOT leak onto the wire.

   Failure semantics: the helper never panics and never bubbles
   error. `Err(SendError(_))` from broadcast::Sender::send (no
   receivers -- the normal state at startup) logs at debug; any
   future unexpected serialization error logs at warn and returns
   without sending.

2. ws.rs: tightened all logs to `target: "aura::ws"` so Phase 6's
   diagnostic story has a single grep target across publisher and
   forwarder. Added explicit "ws subscriber connected" /
   "ws subscriber disconnected" debug entries on every WS lifecycle
   transition. Lag warning text is now structured under the same
   target.

3. publish_session_summary_updated_event and
   publish_assistant_turn_progress_event are intentionally left
   alone -- they carry extra payload fields and aren't part of the
   structural-equality contract the matcher checks.

Tests
-----
Four new regression tests in event_bus.rs pin the shape:
- user_message_event_payload_shape_is_pinned: asserts the canonical
  five keys, expected values, and that Phase 2 bookkeeping fields
  stay off the wire.
- user_message_event_payload_serializes_missing_ids_as_null: drives
  build_chat_event_payload directly with all-None ids and asserts
  each id key is present and `Value::Null` (not elided).
- assistant_message_end_event_shape_matches_user_message_shape:
  the load-bearing structural-drift guard. Calls both publishers
  with the same ctx, recvs both, and asserts the JSON objects are
  identical apart from `type`.
- publish_with_no_subscribers_does_not_panic: drops the receiver
  before publishing so the SendError path is exercised.

All 4 pass. Full lib suite (463 tests) green. Clippy run produced
no new warnings (12 pre-existing baseline preserved).

Cross-phase notes
-----------------
- Phase 5 (UI matcher in interface/) keys on this exact shape and
  the `aura::ws` tracing target.
- Phase 6 will add UI-side diagnostics that grep against
  `target: "aura::ws"` end-to-end (publisher -> forwarder ->
  client log).
- ChatPersistCtx is unchanged; the new payload struct converts
  ctx.project_id (String) and ctx.project_agent_id (String) to
  Some(&str) and propagates ctx.agent_id (Option<String>) as-is.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-ui): live-update receiver panel on cross-agent messages
rawCommits.body:
Phase 5 of the `send_to_agent` cross-agent UX fix. The receiver agent's
chat panel (both standalone `/agents/<id>` and project-scoped
`/projects/<pid>/agents/<paid>`) failed to live-update after a sender
agent posted into its session — the user had to refresh to see the new
user-message and the assistant reply. Persistence was always fine; the
two bugs lived in the WS-event → history-refetch path on the client.

Bug A — wire-shape parser dropped the new field.
The Phase 4 server change (commit 83752884b) locked the wire shape for
`user_message` / `assistant_message_end` to
`{ session_id, project_id, project_agent_id, agent_id }` and removed
the legacy `agent_instance_id` field for those two types. The WS
parser in `interface/src/stores/event-store/event-store.ts` was still
mapping `raw.agent_instance_id` onto `AuraEvent.agent_id`, so after
Phase 4 those events arrived in the subscriber with `agent_id`
unpopulated (the org-level id was sitting in the discarded
`raw.agent_id` slot).

Fixed by:
- Adding `project_agent_id?: string | null` to `AuraEventBase`.
- Updating `parseAuraEvent` to (a) read the org-level `agent_id` from
  the new top-level field, (b) populate `project_agent_id` from
  `raw.project_agent_id`, and (c) fall back to `raw.agent_instance_id`
  for legacy event types (`session_summary_updated`,
  `assistant_turn_progress`) that have not migrated to the new shape.
- Updating the WS handler to forward `project_agent_id` and the
  corrected `agent_id` into the parser's context.

Bug B — `useChatHistorySync` matcher was too strict.
The inline `matches(event)` function in
`interface/src/hooks/use-chat-history-sync/use-chat-history-sync.ts`
treated `watchSessionId` as exclusive: when set, only events for that
exact session fired the refetch. The receiver project panel without a
`?session=` URL pin (i.e. `watchSessionId` undefined) only matched on
`agent_id` / `agent_instance_id` — and after Bug A both of those were
`undefined` for the new wire shape, so the matcher silently skipped.

Fixed by extracting an exported helper `matchesChatEvent(event, watch)`
with three independent OR-conditions in priority order:
  1. `watchSessionId && event.session_id === watchSessionId`
  2. `watchAgentInstanceId && event.project_agent_id === watchAgentInstanceId`
  3. `watchAgentId && event.agent_id === watchAgentId`
Any matching condition fires the refetch — earlier conditions no
longer block lower-tier matches. The hook delegates to the helper so
the same logic is exercised by direct unit tests.

Tests added to `use-chat-history-sync.test.ts`:
- `matcher_fires_for_session_id_match`
- `matcher_fires_for_project_agent_id_match_when_no_session_pin`
- `matcher_fires_for_agent_id_match_on_standalone_panel`
- `matcher_does_not_fire_for_unrelated_event`
- `parser_populates_project_agent_id_from_new_wire_shape`
- `parser_falls_back_to_legacy_agent_instance_id`

Existing matcher integration tests were updated to emit events with
the post-parse top-level shape (`{ session_id, project_agent_id,
agent_id, content }`), and the now-obsolete "session pin is
exclusive" assertion was removed in favour of the new looser contract.

rawCommits.body:
Pin the diagnostic convention for the `send_to_agent` cross-agent UX
chain so the next "B's UI didn't live-update after A's send_to_agent"
report can be reconstructed end-to-end with a single grep across the
server's structured tracing output and one devtools toggle in the
browser — no re-instrumentation.

Phase 4 (commit 83752884b) locked the WS wire shape and added
`target: "aura::ws"` lifecycle / publisher logs; Phase 3 (commit
6d4b70664) added `target: "aura::cross_agent"` on the persist-task
entry, reply-callback dispatch, and reply-callback failure paths;
Phase 5 (commit 0700ed0cf) exported `matchesChatEvent` and fixed the
post-Phase-4 parser regressions. Phase 6 fills the remaining gaps and
documents the convention.

Server-side trace sites (Rust, tracing):

- `aura::cross_agent` / debug — `persist_task observed harness event`
  in `persist_task::run_persist_loop` after each `rx.recv`, with a
  short stable variant kind ("text_delta", "assistant_message_end",
  …) instead of the full event body. Pairs with the WS publisher
  debug so an operator can see both halves of the
  harness→server→broadcast leg under one filter.

- `aura::cross_agent` / debug — `user_message persisted; publishing
  ws event` in `streaming::open_harness_chat_stream` immediately
  before `publish_user_message_event`. This is the hand-off from
  "HTTP handler accepted the user turn" to "WS broadcast tells the
  receiver UI to refetch".

- `aura::ws` / trace — `forwarding ws message to client` in
  `handlers::ws::handle_ws` per forwarded broadcast frame, with a
  `bytes` field. Trace level so production stays silent unless
  explicitly enabled with `RUST_LOG=aura::ws=trace`.

The full table of `aura::ws` and `aura::cross_agent` log sites,
levels, and messages now lives in
`apps/aura-os-server/src/handlers/agents/chat/CROSS_AGENT_TRACING.md`,
and `event_bus.rs` + `cross_agent_reply.rs` module docs reference it
so future log additions don't drift from the convention.

UI-side diagnostic toggle (TypeScript, console.debug):

- `window.__AURA_DEBUG_CROSS_AGENT__ = true` from devtools unlocks
  two gated `console.debug` lines tagged `[aura.cross-agent]`:

  * `event-store::connectEventSocket` — `ws raw` logs every parsed
    WS frame with the raw payload and the parsed view, so
    Bug-A-style parser regressions (a wire-shape change the parser
    silently drops) are immediately visible.

  * `use-chat-history-sync` subscription — `ws event` logs each
    evaluated chat event with the type, routing ids, watch params,
    and whether the matcher accepted it. Factored through an
    exported `maybeLogCrossAgentEvent` helper so the gate is
    unit-testable without driving the full hook scaffolding.

  No new env var, no new build flag, no new toggle store. When the
  property is undefined / falsy the gate is a `typeof window` check
  plus a single property read — effectively free on the hot path.

Test pin:

- `interface/src/hooks/use-chat-history-sync/use-chat-history-sync.test.ts`
  gets a tight three-test block around `maybeLogCrossAgentEvent`:
  truthy flag fires a `[aura.cross-agent]` `console.debug`,
  undefined flag does not, explicitly-falsy flag does not. The flag
  is cleaned up in `afterEach` so the global doesn't leak into
  other test files. Guards against a future "clean up unused debug
  code" sweep that would silently rip the toggle out.

Operator one-liner that turns the whole server chain on at debug:

  RUST_LOG=aura::ws=debug,aura::cross_agent=debug cargo run -p aura-os-server

Append `,aura::ws=trace` to also see the per-message forwarder log.

Logging-only change; no wire-shape or matcher behavior modified
(Phase 4 / Phase 5 contracts stay locked).

rawCommits.subject: feat(test): integration test for Phase 3 cross-agent reply callback
rawCommits.body:
Phase 7 (final phase) of the `send_to_agent` cross-agent UX fix.
Pins the HTTP-level wire contract that Phases 1-3 collectively
implement, end-to-end through the real chat router.

Three scenarios cover the load-bearing contract:

- `cross_agent_reply_callback_fires_on_assistant_message_end` -
  happy path. POST /api/agents/<B>/events/stream with
  `originating_agent_id: "agent-A"`, FakeHarness emits the
  scripted assistant turn, persist task fires the callback. Pins:
  callback POSTs to `/api/agents/agent-A/events/stream`, depth
  header increments to 1 (inbound default 0), body's
  `originating_agent_id` is JSON null (single-hop fall-off),
  `new_session=false`, content carries the reply text, bearer
  token is propagated.

- `cross_agent_callback_skipped_when_originating_agent_id_missing` -
  pins Phase 2's "no upstream sender => no auto-reply" contract.
  Regular user-typed turn fans out ZERO cross-agent POSTs.

- `cross_agent_callback_skipped_at_max_depth` - pins the
  MAX_CROSS_AGENT_REPLY_DEPTH=4 cycle guard. Inbound
  X-Aura-Cross-Agent-Depth: 4 short-circuits before the
  callback spawns.

Implementation notes:

- Mock A-server: `axum::Router` on a random loopback port. Captures
  method, path, depth header, bearer, and JSON body. Echoes back
  `x-aura-chat-persisted: true` so the fixture stays honest with
  the originator-side header gate in `cross_agent_hook.rs` of the
  sibling aura-harness repo.
- Env serialization: process-wide `StdMutex` guards
  `AURA_SERVER_BASE_URL` so a parallel run within this test binary
  cannot flip the var out from under another test's in-flight
  callback. Other integration tests live in separate test binaries
  (= separate processes) so they cannot collide.
- Harness double: `FakeHarness` scripted with a single TextDelta
  ("Hi there!") + AssistantMessageEnd. Wired onto BOTH
  `state.local_harness` and `state.swarm_harness` so the test does
  not depend on agent B's `machine_type`.
- Scenario builder: a minimal but realistic chat env - mock
  storage, mock billing, mock aura-network (404s every lookup so
  the chat resolver falls back to the local shadow), local agent
  shadow, project shadow, project_agent row.

The seed compiled and all three scenarios passed on the first
run against the current branch state; no helpers in
`tests/common/mod.rs` needed adjustment and no test seed bugs
were uncovered.

All three tests green (`cargo test --test cross_agent_reply_callback_test
-p aura-os-server -- --test-threads=1`).

rawCommits.body:
Cross-agent writes (`send_to_agent` from agent A into agent B) were
invisible on the recipient's chat panel until a manual refresh because:

1. The `useChatHistorySync` hook only force-refetches when its panel is
   mounted, so the WS `user_message` / `assistant_message_end` event

2. The chat-history-store cache stayed fresh under `HISTORY_TTL_MS = 30s`,

mounted once from `main.tsx`. It listens for the chat lifecycle WS
events on the existing event-store bus and calls `invalidateHistory`
on every key shape the inbound event could route to (agent-only,
project + project-agent-id, and the session-scoped variant). The next
`fetchHistory` for any affected key bypasses the TTL short-circuit
and re-hits the server, so the recipient panel paints the new
message as soon as the user navigates to it.

that pin both the id->key mapping (`chatHistoryKeysFromEvent`) and the
end-to-end "WS event -> cache stamped stale" flow, including the
no-op cases (no usable ids, no cached entry, blank ids).

rawCommits.subject: fix(generation): emit synthetic generation_start before upstream open
rawCommits.body:
The frontend's 30s stuck-stream watchdog (`STUCK_THRESHOLD_MS` in
`use-stream-health.ts`) was firing the "Agent paused" pill during
long-running image generations (notably `gpt-image-2`), even though
the request was healthy in flight. Root cause: every generation
handler awaited the upstream POST / harness session open BEFORE
constructing the SSE response, so the SSE wire stayed silent for the
full upstream-open latency. When that exceeded 30s the watchdog
tripped before the first wire byte landed.

Fix: defer the upstream open into a background task and return the
SSE response immediately, with a synthetic `generation_start` frame
as the first event on the wire. The watchdog clock resets the moment
the EventSource opens, regardless of how long the upstream takes to
respond. Upstream failures that previously surfaced as HTTP 4xx/5xx
are now translated to in-band `generation_error` SSE frames since
the HTTP 200 has already been committed by the time they are
observed.

Applied uniformly to:
- `generation/image.rs::open_router_image_stream` (auth'd image,
  direct router HTTP path)
- `generation/harness_stream.rs::open_generation_stream` (auth'd
  video + 3D, harness-backed path)
- `public/generation_common/mod.rs::proxy_public_generation_stream`
  (public image / video / 3D proxy)

Tests assert the first emitted frame is `generation_start` even
when the mock upstream stalls for 5s, and that upstream 4xx surfaces
as in-band `generation_error` after the start frame.

rawCommits.subject: fix(generation): emit 15s heartbeat while upstream router is silent
rawCommits.body:
The previous fix emitted a synthetic `generation_start` as the first
SSE frame so the frontend's 30s stuck-stream watchdog
(`STUCK_THRESHOLD_MS` in `use-stream-health.ts`) reset at t=0. But
the watchdog reads `lastEventAt`, which only bumps on wire-driven
setters — so models like `gpt-image-2` that emit nothing between
the upstream `generation_start` and the final `completed` frame
still left the SSE wire silent for the full render and tripped the
"Agent paused" pill at t≈30s anyway.

Fix: in each generation handler's drain loop, wrap the upstream-
chunk wait in `tokio::time::timeout(15s, ...)`. When the timeout
fires, emit a synthetic `generation_progress` heartbeat with a
mode-specific "Generating image/video/3D model..." message
matching what `GenerationStart` already set, then loop. The
frontend's `setProgressText` setter calls `markStreamProgress`
under the hood (`hooks/stream/store.ts`), so each heartbeat resets
the watchdog clock with no frontend change.

15s is well under the 30s threshold even with network jitter or
scheduler hiccups dropping a tick.

Applied uniformly to:
- `generation/image.rs::run_image_upstream_task`
- `generation/harness_stream.rs::run_harness_generation_task`
- `public/generation_common/mod.rs::run_public_generation_task`

Tests use `tokio::test(start_paused = true)` + `time::advance` to
deterministically verify the heartbeat fires when the mock upstream
holds the SSE body open without sending data.

tool, aura-os-server posts B's reply back into A's chat session as a
follow-up `user_message` so A's loop wakes and reacts. The reply was
landing fine, but it rendered indistinguishably from a real
human-typed prompt — Barret's "Hello back!" showed up in A's chat as
a duplicate of A's own input above the actual answer.

badge so cross-agent messages are unmistakable on both legs of the
round trip:

-----------
- `SendChatRequest.from_agent_id` (additive, `#[serde(default)]`):

  another agent rather than typed by a human.
- `ChatPersistCtx.from_agent_id` threads the field from

  persist hot path.
- `persist_user_message` embeds `from_agent_id` into the persisted

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): stabilize image-generation ETA so the countdown only ticks downward
rawCommits.body:
The early `generation_progress.percent` frames from the upstream
router land in tight bursts and the adaptive
`elapsed * (100 - percent) / percent` formula can briefly project a
total well above the per-model baseline (the reported symptom was a
`gpt-image-2` countdown that jumped from ~0:50 up to 1:13 before
settling and ticking down normally). The remaining time was
recomputed from scratch on every tick, so any noisy percent value
visibly bounced the digits.

Latch the projected completion timestamp in a ref scoped to the
current run (`startedAt`-bound): seed it from the very first
estimate, then ratchet it down only when a new estimate points to a
sooner completion. Later projections — whether from a noisy
adaptive update or a sub-threshold percent — are ignored, so the
countdown never jumps upward and `Math.max(0, completion - now)`
counts smoothly to zero. A `startedAt` change (second send on the
same entry) resets the latch so a retry doesn't inherit the
previous run's floor and read as immediately overrun.

Adds two regression tests: one pins the never-jump-upward contract
across multiple noisy percent updates, the other guards the latch
reset on a fresh run. Updates the pre-existing
"sub-threshold percent ignored" test to assert the new latched
behavior (the previous value persists instead of reverting to the
baseline, which is strictly more correct).

rawCommits.subject: refactor(stream): move ETA latch from useRef to useState (first-render stability)
rawCommits.body:
The monotonic-latch in `useGenerationEta` was implemented with a
`useRef` mutated during render. That works for steady-state
countdowns but is hostile to React's render model: the mutation is
not part of the dependency graph, so any concurrent / Strict-mode
double render would observe a candidate-only value before the ref
seeded itself, briefly flashing an out-of-order ETA.

This rewrites the latch using `useState` synced via a dedicated
`useEffect`. To keep the first render correct before the effect has
a chance to seed the latch, the displayed value is
`min(latchedForThisRun, candidate)`:

- `latchedForThisRun` defaults to `+Infinity` when the latch hasn't
  caught up to the current `startedAt` yet, so the candidate wins on
  the very first render of a new run.
- On every subsequent render the latch can only ratchet downward
  (sync effect drops upward candidates), so the displayed value is
  monotonically non-increasing for the lifetime of a single run.

Behaviour observable to the user is unchanged — countdown still
ticks downward only — but the implementation no longer relies on
in-render ref mutation.

The three latch transitions (cleared / new run / sooner candidate)
are documented inline so the next reader doesn't have to reverse
the state machine from the conditionals.

rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): pin RUSTC to dtolnay toolchain on Windows so sccache stops mixing rustc versions
rawCommits.body:
The windows-latest runner image now preinstalls rustc 1.95.0 alongside
our dtolnay-installed 1.94.1. The recent PATH-pin step wrote an
MSYS-style "/c/Users/runneradmin/.rustup/toolchains/<tc>/bin" entry to
$GITHUB_PATH, which native Windows PATH lookups silently ignore, so
Cargo and `sccache rustc` fell through to the system 1.95.0. Combined
with the restored `../.aura-shared-target` and the Depot WebDAV sccache
backend, the same `cargo build` ended up with 1.94.1 rmeta files (e.g.
liblazy_static-d4e740f22aab7745.rmeta) sitting next to crates being
driven by 1.95.0, tripping E0514 ("found crate compiled by an
incompatible version of rustc") on every Desktop Nightly Windows run
since the image bump.

Fix the pin both ways:
- Convert the toolchain bin dir with `cygpath -w` before writing to
  $GITHUB_PATH on Windows so native PATH lookups actually honor it.
- Export RUSTC, CARGO, and RUSTDOC as absolute Windows paths into the
  pinned toolchain. Cargo forwards $RUSTC verbatim to $RUSTC_WRAPPER,
  so this also pins the binary sccache invokes -- no further PATH
  ambiguity is possible.

Also bump `shared-key` (desktop, desktop-app, desktop-sidecar -> *-v2)
on the three workflows that share `../.aura-shared-target` so the
existing cache, which already contains 1.94.1-tagged rmeta files
produced under the broken pin, is not restored on the next run. The
first run after this merges will rebuild Windows from scratch; later
runs will hit the v2 cache populated entirely with the truly-pinned
1.94.1 artifacts.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rendered.title: Public mode launches and cross-agent chat becomes legible
rendered.intro: A big day for Aura: anonymous visitors can now try Code, Plan, Image, Video, and 3D directly from a new logged-out shell, cross-agent messages finally route and render correctly end-to-end, and a long tail of fixes tightened the Windows terminal, embedded browser error pages, image-generation ETAs, and the macOS/Windows release pipelines.

entries.title: Windows terminal, themed browser errors, and chat bubble polish
entries.summary: A dense afternoon of UI and platform fixes spanning the in-app terminal on Windows, the embedded browser's error handling, and a refresh of chat bubble styling and copy behavior.

items.text: Rewrote the Windows in-app terminal: PTY spawn now waits for xterm.js to measure its container, PSReadLine is removed on launch, and a Ctrl+L safety net wipes scrollback locally — eliminating the cursor-jumping, overlapping-text, and broken `clear`/`cls` bugs on PowerShell.

The embedded browser now paints Aura's themed error overlay for HTTP 4xx/5xx as well as network failures, and the overlay survives Chromium's native error-page commit, address-bar reloads, and the initial-navigation race that previously hid it until refresh.

Chat user bubbles now follow the active accent (with per-theme contrast), got rounder corners and a shorter footprint, and gained a hover-revealed copy button; assistant copy and spec/large-text blocks now preserve markdown source on the clipboard while still pasting as formatted text into rich editors.

Floating popovers across the app now share the panel background instead of looking like a lighter elevated shelf, terminal selection follows the accent color, and the Context popover hydrates its per-bucket breakdown immediately on chat mount instead of waiting for the next turn.

Sidekick terminals now show a browser-style tab strip with always-visible session tabs, an inline `+`, and per-session close — backed by a shared `InstanceTabs` primitive used by both browser and terminal panes; the env-overlay also refreshes the Workspace Folder row after project/agent saves instead of waiting for a manual reload.
Hardened the macOS parity gate so it stops misidentifying Homebrew's rustup-init shim as `rustc 1.29.0`, walking PATH and validating the version banner before accepting a candidate.

entries.title: Anthropic 529 retries in the changelog generator
entries.summary: Release tooling becomes resilient to upstream overload errors.

items.text: The daily changelog generator now retries Anthropic Messages API calls with exponential backoff, full jitter, and retry-after handling, so a single `overloaded_error` no longer fails the Publish/Reconcile Release Changelog job.

entries.title: Faster, quieter Windows desktop updates
entries.summary: The desktop updater stops flashing a console window on Windows and surfaces new releases much sooner.

items.text: Fixed a visible console flash on every Windows update handoff by dropping `DETACHED_PROCESS` so `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` is honored and child apps inherit the hidden console.

The titlebar Update pill and Settings Update control now re-check for releases on window focus / tab visibility (with a 60s cooldown), and the desktop poll interval drops from 30 minutes to 5 minutes, so returning to Aura after a release ships surfaces the pill almost instantly.

entries.title: Taming the Homebrew rustup shim on macOS CI
entries.summary: A focused thread of CI fixes that finally pinned the right Rust toolchain on macos-latest runners and stopped a parallel sccache install race.

items.text: Replaced the seven `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` usages across the desktop-validate, release-nightly, and release-stable workflows with a new composite `setup-rust-toolchain` action that probes `RUSTUP_HOME/toolchains/<tc>/bin` directly and prepends it to `$GITHUB_PATH`, so `cargo` / `rustc` / `clippy-driver` on macos-latest stop resolving to Homebrew's broken rustup-init shim.

The new setup action also scrubs stale `lib/rustlib/src` trees and exports `RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0` to prevent parallel sccache rustc invocations from racing rustup into a `rust-src` reinstall conflict mid-build.

entries.title: Logged-out public mode, cross-agent chat, and image-generation ETAs
entries.summary: The day's largest batch: a brand-new anonymous web shell with rate-limited Code/Plan/Image/Video/3D, the final phases of the cross-agent messaging fix, and a series of fixes to image generation streaming and its on-screen countdown.

items.text: Shipped an end-to-end logged-out public mode: a new slim shell at `/` with sessions panel, marketing footer, and the promoted `features/chat-ui` input bar lets anonymous web visitors run up to 3 turns of Code, Plan, Image, Video, or 3D against a system-owned demo agent before hitting a non-dismissable 'Thanks for trying AURA' modal. Backed by guest JWTs, a per-guest/per-IP rate limiter behind a `Clock` trait, hardcoded cheap server-side defaults, and an `AURA_PUBLIC_GENERATION_ENABLED` kill-switch for the expensive endpoints.

Ported the aura-website Product, Changelog, Feedback, and Pricing pages into a new `MarketingShell` mounted on logged-out routes, and reworked the logged-out chat empty state into an inline `ComposePanel` with five example prompts, a `LoginOverlay` modal over the shell, a Logout entry in the File menu, and a titlebar layout that now keeps native window controls reachable.

Finished the cross-agent `send_to_agent` fix: the server now posts agent B's reply back into agent A's session as a follow-up turn with depth-guarded, UTF-8-safe fire-and-forget delivery; the WebSocket wire shape is locked and documented; the receiving panel's history matcher and global cache invalidator live-update without a refresh; and a new `from_agent_id` field drives a '↩ from <agent>' badge so cross-agent messages stop looking like duplicate user prompts.

Generation streams no longer trip the 30s 'Agent paused' watchdog on long renders: handlers emit a synthetic `generation_start` as the very first SSE frame, send a 15s heartbeat while the upstream router is silent, and the on-bubble image ETA was retuned twice — first to a stable monotonic latch, then to a simple linear countdown from a per-model baseline (with `gpt-image-2` bumped to 120s) so the digits stop snapping to 'Almost done...'.

Logged-out polish: session delete (X) is now a real sibling button (no more nested-interactive HTML) and hops to the next remaining session instead of spawning a fresh empty chat, mode-pill clicks keep the textarea focused, the login form auto-focuses and selects the email field on entry, and visiting the login modal no longer mints an empty 'New chat' row on every round-trip.

Auth now rehosts zOS Matrix `mxc://` profile pictures into Aura's S3 bucket on first sync (one-time per user, never overwriting Aura-uploaded avatars) so frontends get a permanent URL alongside the existing display-name sync.

Small chat polish: the assistant bubble's copy button now sits left of the leading Block chevron instead of covering Thought/File/Spec headers, and the input bar's stray '·' divider is hidden on projectless chats where the orbit indicator renders nothing.

entries.title: Windows release builds stop mixing rustc 1.94.1 and 1.95.0
entries.summary: Late-evening fix to the Windows half of the desktop release pipeline after a runner-image bump introduced a parallel rustc.

items.text: Pinned `RUSTC`, `CARGO`, and `RUSTDOC` to the dtolnay-installed toolchain on Windows runners using `cygpath -w` so native PATH lookups honor it, stopping `sccache rustc` from falling through to the runner image's preinstalled rustc 1.95.0 and tripping E0514 against 1.94.1 rmeta files; shared-key suffixes were bumped to `*-v2` so the poisoned cache is not restored.
